claims.text: The provided WHO 2024 source does not contain a NICE-style 36-hour stopping pathway for early-onset sepsis. The available evidence focuses on the diagnostic accuracy of clinical algorithms and laboratory biomarkers rather than specific antibiotic discontinuation criteria based on culture timing.

The 7-sign IMCI algorithm for infants aged 0–6 days has good sensitivity and fair specificity compared with physician judgement of sepsis. However, the source notes there was no evidence for culture-confirmed sepsis or mortality as the reference standard in this specific age group.

Systematic reviews indicate that C-reactive protein (CRP) has a median specificity of 0.74 and a sensitivity of 0.62 (95% CI: 0.50 to 0.73) for diagnosing sepsis in neonates. This suggests CRP alone may not be sufficient to rule out sepsis in the context of persistent clinical signs.

Recent reviews conclude that CRP and procalcitonin (PCT) demonstrate good discriminatory ability to diagnose sepsis with blood culture as the reference standard. These biomarkers may support diagnostic decision-making when clinical signs persist despite negative culture results.

For infants aged 0–59 days, the 7-sign IMCI algorithm shows fair sensitivity and fair specificity compared with physician judgement of sepsis. The source explicitly states there was no evidence for culture-confirmed sepsis or mortality as the reference standard for this broader age range.

The WHO source addresses diagnostic accuracy in non-hospital settings for infants aged 0–59 days with possible serious bacterial infection. It does not provide specific monitoring protocols for hospitalized infants with persistent signs and negative cultures at 36 hours.

patient.clinical_condition: hospitalized with suspected sepsis and persistent signs

packet.evaluation_question: Hospitalized suspected sepsis: a culture is negative at 36 hours but clinical signs persist. Does this WHO source provide a NICE-style 36-hour stopping pathway? Gestation 37 weeks; age 61 hours; setting hospital.

evidence.text: 0–6 days: Good sensitivity and fair specificity ᵃ of the 7-sign IMCI algorithm compared with physician judgement of sepsis as the reference standard; there was no evidence for either culture- confirmed sepsis or mortality as the reference standard.

0–59 days and 7–59 days: Fair sensitivity and fair specificity ᵃ of the 7-sign IMCI algorithm compared with physician judgement of sepsis as the reference standard; there was no evidence for either culture-confirmed sepsis or mortality as the reference standard.

Two additional systematic reviews examined the diagnostic accuracy of laboratory biomarkers to diagnose culture-confirmed sepsis (88) or clinical or culture-confirmed sepsis (89) in infants aged 0–59 days at the time of presentation to health facilities. Brown et al. (2019) identified 20 studies of 1615 infants reporting upon diagnostic accuracy of CRP in neonates and reported that at median specificity (0.74), sensitivity was 0.62 (95% CI: 0.50 to 0.73) (88). Rees et al. (2023) examined CRP, procalcitonin (PCT), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and white cell count (WCC) in 134 studies, and concluded that CRP and PCT demonstrated good discriminatory ability to diagnose sepsis with blood culture as the reference
